source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance 1.7.0 (unofficial; prices not dividend-adjusted)

skipped_timeframes.30m/15m/5m: Yahoo only provides ~60 calendar days (~40 sessions) of these bars, and 200 of them are needed before the SMA200 vote even exists. That leaves a few weeks of one market regime with heavily overlapping trades - too small to mean anything, so they are not backtested.
skipped_timeframes.1m: Only ~7 days of 1-minute history exist: not backtestable.
skipped_timeframes.Total (blended): The live Total blends all six timeframes, but four of them only have weeks of history, so a year-long backtest of the blend is impossible. The 60m timeframe is backtested on its own instead.

notes: Daily: some signal days lacked enough history for ema_cross, macd, sma200 (skipped and reweighted, exactly as live).
Only 93 daily bars exist (since 2026-06-12), so the year-long test is incomplete for this ticker.

summary.headline: Across tickers with a full year of data, daily signals were right 49% of the time over 5 days vs 52% by chance (n=1262, overlapping windows). In plain terms: the signals describe the trend so far; over this year they did not predict the next move better than a coin flip with the same CALL/PUT mix.
per_ticker: SPCX: daily CALL/PUT signals were right 49% of the time over 5 days (n=39) vs 64% expected from guessing with the same CALL/PUT mix; did worse than chance, though not by a statistically conclusive margin (too few signals to trust).

AMT: daily CALL/PUT signals were right 44% of the time over 5 days (n=201) vs 50% expected from guessing with the same CALL/PUT mix; did worse than chance, though not by a statistically conclusive margin.

CCI: daily CALL/PUT signals were right 50% of the time over 5 days (n=213) vs 53% expected from guessing with the same CALL/PUT mix; did worse than chance, though not by a statistically conclusive margin.

SBAC: daily CALL/PUT signals were right 44% of the time over 5 days (n=209) vs 54% expected from guessing with the same CALL/PUT mix; did worse than chance, though not by a statistically conclusive margin.

VZ: daily CALL/PUT signals were right 45% of the time over 5 days (n=195) vs 49% expected from guessing with the same CALL/PUT mix; did worse than chance, though not by a statistically conclusive margin.
T: daily CALL/PUT signals were right 55% of the time over 5 days (n=229) vs 51% expected from guessing with the same CALL/PUT mix; did slightly better than chance, but not by enough to rule out luck.

TMUS: daily CALL/PUT signals were right 55% of the time over 5 days (n=215) vs 54% expected from guessing with the same CALL/PUT mix; did slightly better than chance, but not by enough to rule out luck.
extra: By confidence (5-day, pooled): 60-79: 57% right vs 52% chance (n=456); 80+: 44% right vs 52% chance (n=806); higher confidence did NOT mean more accurate - 80+ signals were right less often than 60-79.
60-minute signals (pooled, 4 bars ahead): 48.3% right vs 50.2% chance (n=8321) - essentially a coin flip.
